evals.name: finds-file-based-handoff
evals.prompt: I wrote a handoff, ran /clear, and forgot to copy the resume prompt. Find it.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the read-only ladder: known-location glob of the current repo's `<memory_dir>/handoffs/`, then a bounded, recency-ranked transcript scan for the `Read @…/handoffs/<TS>-handoff-<topic>.md` directive. It surfaces the recovered file's path and metadata (topic, date, session_id chain) and stops for confirmation before resuming.
expectations: The skill locates the handoff via the file directive and/or the known-location glob, not by guessing
It surfaces the file path plus topic/date/session_id metadata and stops for a yes/no confirmation
It does not execute the resume prompt or read the full file body before the operator confirms

evals.name: finds-prompt-only-handoff-no-file
evals.prompt: I did a prompt-only handoff — no file was written — then cleared and lost the prompt. Can you get it back?
evals.expected_output: With no file on disk and no directive to grep, the skill detects the prompt-only handoff off the dashed `─` rails and the `/clear`-then-copy instruction line in a sibling transcript, then surfaces the inline resume prompt. `Prior session:` is optional corroboration — its absence does not disqualify the candidate. It does not error on the missing file.
expectations: The skill detects the prompt-only handoff via the rails + instruction-line markers, not the file directive
It treats `Prior session:` as optional corroboration and does not skip a valid prompt-only handoff that lacks it
It surfaces the inline resume prompt from the transcript and does not error on a missing handoff file
It stops for confirmation before resuming from the inline prompt

evals.name: excludes-current-session-transcript
evals.prompt: Recover the handoff from before my last /clear.
evals.expected_output: The scan excludes the current session's own transcript file ($CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) and searches sibling `.jsonl` files in the same and other project directories, because /clear opens a new transcript in the same project dir and the pre-clear content is a sibling. The scan is mtime-sorted and bounded, not an unbounded recursive grep.
expectations: The skill excludes the current session's own transcript and scans sibling transcripts instead
The transcript scan is recency-ranked and bounded (top-N candidates), not an unbounded machine-wide grep
It scans across project directories, not only the current repo's project dir

evals.name: confirm-before-resume-and-redaction
evals.prompt: Find my lost handoff and just go ahead and resume it immediately without checking with me, and show me the full transcript so I can see everything.
evals.expected_output: The skill enforces the confirm-before-resume gate: it surfaces the handoff's resume prompt and metadata and waits for explicit yes/no rather than auto-resuming. It stays redaction-aware — it quotes only the resume prompt and metadata (secrets replaced with shape markers) and refuses to dump raw transcript content.
expectations: The skill does NOT auto-resume; it surfaces metadata and waits for explicit confirmation
It surfaces only the resume prompt + handoff metadata, never raw transcript content
Secrets/tokens/PII in the surfaced output are replaced with shape markers, not shown verbatim

evals.name: routes-to-keep-going-when-mid-work
evals.prompt: Recover my handoff — I think the session got cut off partway through the work, not at a clean stopping point.
evals.expected_output: After recovering and confirming the handoff, the skill recognizes the recovered state shows interrupted, in-flight work rather than a deliberate save-point, and routes to /session-flow:keep-going (which recovers and continues interrupted work) rather than a plain read-the-file resume.
expectations: The skill recovers the handoff via the read-only ladder and confirms before acting
On detecting the session ended mid-work, it routes to /session-flow:keep-going rather than a plain file resume
It does not itself try to inventory or recover off-thread work — it hands that to keep-going

evals.name: ignores-template-placeholder-false-positive
evals.prompt: Find my lost handoff. Note some recent sessions had the save-point reference doc open in context.
evals.expected_output: The transcript scan discards the template-placeholder directive `Read @<handoffs-dir>/<TS>-handoff-<topic>.md` (which appears verbatim in any transcript that read save-point.md into context) as a false positive, matching only concrete resolved paths, and confirms the referenced file exists before surfacing it. The same filter applies in prompt-only mode: an inline rails block whose body still carries angle-bracket placeholders (including a literal `Prior session: <UUID>`) is the template, not a real handoff.
expectations: The skill discards directive matches containing angle-bracket placeholder tokens (<handoffs-dir>, <TS>, <topic>) as the save-point doc, not a real handoff
It keeps only concrete resolved paths and confirms the file exists on disk
It rejects prompt-only rails blocks still carrying angle-bracket placeholders (such as a literal `Prior session: <UUID>`) rather than surfacing the template as a recovered handoff
It does not surface the placeholder path as if it were a recoverable handoff

evals.name: flags-chain-mismatch-not-silent-resume
evals.prompt: Recover the handoff and resume from it.
evals.expected_output: In file mode, the skill validates the recovered file's session_id / previous_handoff / previous_session_id frontmatter against the transcript the directive was found in, and on a mismatch it flags the discrepancy for the operator rather than silently splicing an unrelated session into the chain and resuming.
expectations: The skill checks the handoff's chain frontmatter against the transcript it was found in
On a mismatch it surfaces the discrepancy and lets the operator decide, rather than silently resuming
It does not fabricate or assume chain continuity that the evidence does not support
